verdict.reasoning: Headache for about a day: 'Had it for about a day now.' Left-sided: 'Mainly on the left side.' Throbbing: 'just, yeah, kind of throbbing headache.' Photophobia: 'Kind of seems to be worse when I'm in a light room or like sunlight.' Severity described as 'really bad headache,' supporting severe.

Duration and character: 'Had it for about a day now... kind of throbbing.' Left-sided: 'Mainly on the left side.' Photophobia: 'worse when I'm in a light room or like sunlight.' Intermittent but not fully resolving: 'Just kind of fade? So it's still there a little bit, but it kind of gets more or less severe.'
Onset: 'Yeah, just since yesterday morning, Since I woke up, really.'
Positional improvement: 'Does it get worse with any position...?' Patient: 'No, I think I've generally been lying down. Seems to be better that way.'

Position/cough: 'Does it get worse with any position...?' Patient: 'No...' and 'Any problems if you cough or sneeze?' Patient: 'No, but I haven't really got a cough or anything.' This supports not worsened by position or cough/Valsalva.
Visual changes: 'Any problems with your eyes or your eyesight?' Patient: 'No, not at all.'
Focal neuro: 'And any problems with weakness, tingling, numbness in your arms or legs?' Patient: 'No, not at all.'
Abnormal smells/tastes: 'Any abnormal smells or tastes?' Patient: 'No.'
Nausea/vomiting: 'Any. Any nausea, vomiting?' Patient: 'No, no, I've been feeling fine, actually.'

Fever: When asked about feverish/temperature, patient says: 'No, not really... I was doing okay the day before.' She also says: 'I don't feel like I'm feverish, but I haven't checked.' This supports denial of fever.

URTI symptoms: 'Have you had any other symptoms like feeling feverish, temperature, any runny nose, sore ears? ... Any sort of cold symptoms?' Patient: 'No, not really... I was doing okay the day before.'
Skin: 'Have you had any changes in your skin?' Patient: 'No, skin's been fine.'

No prior similar headaches: 'Normally, do you get any headaches?' Patient: 'No, not really. It's not something I've ever had before.' Later: 'this headache is new to you and you've not had regular headaches before?' Patient: 'Yeah.'

Possible trigger stress: 'Has anything changed recently or any. Anything you've done recently might have triggered it?' Patient: 'Not I can think of maybe a bit stressed out of work, that kind of thing.'
Menses: 'has it occurred at a particular time in your menstrual cycle?' Patient: 'No, not particularly. My period was about a week ago.'
Past medical/surgical history: 'In the past, have you had any significant medical problems? Any hospital admissions, operations, anything like that?' Patient: 'No, not recently. Nothing.'
Contraceptive: 'And which contraception do you take?' Patient: 'Microgynon.' 'When did you start that one?' Patient: 'About six years ago.'
Paracetamol PRN: 'What tablets have you been taking already for it?' Patient: 'Just paracetamol.' This supports use as needed for this headache.
Aspirin reaction: 'I'm allergic to aspirin, so I haven't been taking that.' Doctor: 'What happens when you take aspirin?' Patient: 'I just feel really sick.'
Family history HTN: 'Anyone in your family had any medical problems?' Patient: 'My mum had high blood pressure...'
Family history migraine: Same sentence: 'My mum had high blood pressure and she's got a history of migraines.'
Living situation: 'Who do you live with at home?' Patient: 'Just with housemates, just friends.'
Alcohol: 'Do you drink much alcohol day today?' Patient: 'I'd say a normal amount probably, you know, a few drinks at the weekend.'
Smoking: 'Do you smoke?' Patient: 'No.'
Drugs: 'Do you take any other drugs of any sort?' Patient: 'No.'

Clinical assessment: New unilateral throbbing headache with photophobia is documented. Doctor: 'I mean from the sounds of it, it does sound quite like a migraine, but obviously even had no history of that in the past.' No red flags noted and no strong secondary cause discussed, supporting low suspicion for secondary cause.
Aspirin intolerance: As above, aspirin causes nausea: 'I'm allergic to aspirin... I just feel really sick.' This supports an intolerance rather than classic allergic features.

NSAID with paracetamol, avoid aspirin: 'What I would suggest is taking some anti inflammatories along with a paracetamol.' Given documented aspirin intolerance, avoidance of aspirin is implicit and already stated by patient.

Hydration is advised: 'Make sure you're really well hydrated.' However, resting specifically 'in a dark room' is never mentioned; only that light worsens symptoms and she has been staying in, so explicit advice for a dark room is an addition.

BP and thermometer: 'I would try and manage to get your blood pressure checked if you haven't had a chat for a while.' and 'Another thing to do is to have a thermometer at home so you make sure that your temperature is okay.' Location (pharmacy/GP) is implied but not specified; overall content is supported.

Red-flag advice: 'if it isn't settling or it's getting worse or you get any other change in your headache or you're unwell with it with a high temperature, then we would certainly need to speak to you straight away...' and later 'If you have a raised temperature or headaches just getting worse and we develop any rashes or anything like that, then we'd need to speak to you straight away.' Neurological deficits are not explicitly mentioned but worsening/change in headache covers serious progression; overall red-flag advice is present.

Reassessment for recurrent/patterned headaches: 'if you're getting persistent headaches or headaches associated with your menstrual cycle or sexual, certain things seem to trigger these headaches, then it would be worth having a further discussion about it to see whether we can work out if we can help that longer term.'
